00:00:04 Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining on time, um this is Maya from Redwood, i'll kick us off. Rafael is with me from solutions. Jason, Priya, nice to see you all.
00:00:22 Jason Park (Alder Grid): Hi Maya, thanks. Yeah we wanted to go over renewal numbers and also see where we could tighten latency for our chat product before the Q3 launch.
00:00:40 Rafael (Redwood SE): yeah hi all, i'll be technical lead for this call, i'll go through the benchmark plan and a couple quick wins like kv cache and batch sizing.

00:01:25 Sofia (Alder Grid): yes internal approvals, legal redlines etc, target to sign by mid-July but we need the final pro-forma by early next week so finance can review.
00:01:48 Maya: perfect, we'll send that by Friday.
00:01:55 Liam (Alder Grid): on infra side, our peering to APAC region is in place but we need the dedicated pool or edge nodes closer to our customers, otherwise tail latency spikes.
00:02:12 Rafael: understood. so our options are: 1) hosted route with APAC region + caching, 2) dedicated capacity in ap-east, or 3) private VPC with a local edge pilot. each has trade-offs on cost and SLAs.
00:02:35 Jason: can you remind me what the cost delta is between hosted and dedicated for our current profile? we saw a big increase on the last renewal.
00:02:50 Maya: yes, so with dedicated you get reserved GPUs and better per-token economics at sustained QPS; hosted is burstable but unit price is higher. we'll include a tiered table in the new pro-forma showing break-even at different sustained throughput levels.
00:03:12 Priya: and what about fallback behavior? if the dedicated pool is saturated, will you route to hosted?
00:03:22 Rafael: yes we can configure smart routing: primary to dedicated, fallback to hosted or a smaller model variant. can do model pinning and automatic fallback thresholds. could show you logs of a similar customer if that helps.
00:03:40 Priya: that would help.
00:03:45 Maya: we'll include an example trace.
00:03:50 Jason: security is another ask — SOC2 and KMS integration. have those docs been updated?
00:04:00 Rafael: we have updated SOC2 Type II report and a KMS integration guide. some small differences depending on hosted vs private. we'll push artifacts to the SSO share.
00:04:15 Sofia: please include key rotations policy and audit log retention in the packet.
00:04:22 Rafael: will do.
00:04:30 Maya: ok let's move to the latency optimization runbook. Rafael, want to go through the recommended quick wins?
00:04:38 Rafael: sure. first, prefix/KV caching — ensuring your common system prompts are cached reduces first-token latency by up to 30% for us in similar workloads. second, tuning batch size based on request size distribution; we recommend dynamic batching with a 20ms window for bursty chat. third, model quantization profiles — using FP16 or 4-bit quant for non-critical assistant flows can cut token cost with minimal accuracy loss.
00:05:10 Liam: the KV cache sounds promising — does that require any client changes?
00:05:16 Rafael: minimal. you can either push a sticky key in the header or let our SDK persist a session token. there is a small SDK change but we can provide a patch.
00:05:27 Priya: for quant profiles, we need to run evals against our safety prompts — can you help with that?
00:05:33 Rafael: yes we'll include a test harness and a baseline eval set. we'll also recommend fallbacks to higher-precision variants for sensitive routes.
00:05:44 Jason: timeline — we need a pilot in APAC by mid-July, is that realistic?
00:05:52 Maya: tight but possible. Rafael, what do you need to get the APAC edge pilot ready?
00:05:58 Rafael: access to sample traffic, an infra contact for whitelisting egress, and SLA targets. ideally we run a 48-hour benchmark using their sample workload and measure p95/p99.
00:06:13 Priya: we can provide sample traffic and our p95 target is <120ms for chat end-to-end excluding client render.
00:06:23 Rafael: noted — we'll aim for p95 <120ms in the APAC edge pilot. we'll also document configuration: batch window, cache TTLs, model variant mapping.
00:06:35 Maya: procurement — Sofia, we'll send the pro-forma and the security bundle. any constraints on invoicing or PO number?
00:06:42 Sofia: PO standard, we need vendor details and line item codes. legal may request a clause update on indemnity; i'll flag that now.
00:06:55 Maya: ok we'll route legal to your counsel.
00:07:00 Jason: competitor question — we tested PineCloud last quarter and they were cheaper but had 10-20ms worse p95 in our region, so cost vs latency is key.
00:07:13 Rafael: that's typical; our smart routing and prefix cache usually closes that gap. we can show a side-by-side with their public benchmarks.
00:07:25 Priya: also curious about private deployment — we might need on-prem for regulated customers, is that in scope for this renewal?
00:07:34 Maya: we can add private deployment as an add-on for the term, with separate pricing. for now pilot in APAC edge should cover 70-80% of our use-case.
00:07:45 Liam: on-prem is heavier — we'd need KMS/HSM support and audit hooks; what's Redwood's story there?
00:07:52 Rafael: we support customer-managed KMS HSM and audit forwarding; there's an optional on-prem package with air-gapped deploys. we'll surface the whitepaper.
00:08:03 Jason: ok good. let's capture next steps.
